reading.title: Pocket Money
reading.text: Every Saturday, Dilnoza gets pocket money from her parents. She used to spend all of it on sweets and stickers, but now she tries to save money. Last month she wanted a new football, but she was a bit short of money. So she borrowed a little from her brother and promised to pay him back in cash. To earn money, she also washes the family car on Sundays. She thinks it is a waste of money to buy things she does not really need.

reading.title: Saving for the Future
reading.text: Mr Karimov worked hard for forty years. He never made a fortune, but he always put some money into savings. When his friend got into debt, Mr Karimov did not lend him money at once. Instead, he explained how to plan a budget. His friend slowly paid off the debt in three years. Now Mr Karimov has a savings account with enough money for a small house. He says that the best way to avoid debt is to spend less than you earn.

reading.title: A Good Bargain
reading.text: Last weekend Tom went shopping for a jacket. The first shop had a nice one, but the price was very high. He looked at the price tag twice and left. In the second shop, prices were lower, and there was a sale at half price on winter clothes. Tom found a warm jacket at a reasonable price, only thirty dollars. The shop assistant said that prices usually fall at the end of the season. Tom was happy because he did not want to buy it at any price.
